lines: Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.
Nosuri — `voice_criticality: medium`. Fora-da-lei atrevida e malandra; "aliada da justiça" irônica; oportunista. Registro coloquial/esperto.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

lines.source: Whew... We've walked a fair bit now.
Hey, bosslady. About how far are we now?
I think we should be seeing the road soon.
This took much longer than we anticipated.
Well, we can't help it, with these bumpy and\n
winding roads...
Perhaps it would behoove us to hurry. Our\n
progress will stall if we do not arrive by\n
nightfall.
Yeah, you're right. Let's pick up the pace,\n
everyone. Gotta get there before it gets dark.
Just as I try to rally the rest of the group\n
forward, the twins suddenly stop me.
Wait.
Please be careful, Master. Something is drawing\n
near.
What...?
At the twins' words, Jachdwalt immediately\n
lowers himself down to put his ear to the\n
ground.
...Footsteps. Not just one or two people,\n
either. Whole lot of 'em on the way.
Tuskur soldiers?
Safe bet.
A sudden anxiety hangs in the air with\n
Jachdwalt's words.
Wh-What do we do? At this rate, we're going to\n
run right into them...
We should turn back! Now!
We cannot turn around so easily on such a\n
narrow road...
We may easily hide ourselves, but concealing\n
these carts would be nigh impossible.
Then can we... take care of them?
Atuy eagerly readies her spear. Faces grim,\n
Nosuri and Jachdwalt begin drawing their own\n
weapons.
Hold on, hold on! We haven't been found out yet.
I hastily try to calm everyone down.
The Tuskur army must be using this road to\n
ambush the Yamatan forces.
I'm sorry, Haku... I didn't--
Hey, don't worry. This path was our only shot\n
anyways, and I'm glad you told us about it.
Haku...
The Tuskur army knows this path is here.\n
I figured there was a chance something like this\n
would happen.
Well, ain't that reassurin'.
It sounds like you've already got a plan in that\n
clever head of yours, eh, love?
I knew it could happen... I just hoped it\n
wouldn't come to this.
Kuon, you said that only the locals know about\n
this path, right?
Huh? Yes...
Then... I might have an idea.
You do, Haku!?
It's gonna be risky, though.\n
Listen up, everybody.
I'm pretty sure the Tuskur army isn't expecting\n
any Yamatans on this path.
So their first assumption would be that only\n
other people from Tuskur would use this road.
A sound enough theory...
Luckily, we're not real soldiers of Yamato.\n
No uniforms or anything. We might just be able\n
to fool them.
Even if we defeat them, it won't make our job\n
any easier. Let's hide our weapons, and play it\n
cool!
As I'm explaining all this, I sneak a glance\n
at Kuon.
I want to avoid bloodshed wherever possible\n
here.
Gotcha. Guess we'll go with the boss's plan\n
then, yeah?
It is the best course of action we've come up\n
with so far.
Yes. If we can get through this without having\n
to fight, that would be the best outcome for\n
all.
But do you really think this is going to work?
Well if it doesn't, then we just take care of\n
them, right?
I-I suppose.
Still feeling uneasy, we shift the carts to the\n
roadside. Eventually, in the distance...
Just like we expected...
Fully-armed soldiers of Tuskur.
They idly chat among themselves as they close in\n
on us.
Judging by how relaxed they are, they might be\n
on patrol or just heading to an assigned post.
Maybe their guards will be down if they don't\n
expect the Yamatans to have found this path...
They seem too deep in conversation at first, but\n
then they notice us clustered around the carts.
Tuskur soldier
Hm? Who are all of you...?
The man at the front, their apparent leader,\n
eyes us warily as he speaks.
Argh, just gonna have to wing it...!
I hunch slightly and put my hands together,\n
striding toward their leader with a booming\n
voice.
Heh hyeh hyeh! A most delightful and rejuvenating\n
morning to you, my good sir!
And you would be...?
Y-Yes, ah, the big cheeses over at the fortress\n
needed supplies delivered, so we're on the job!
The fortress, hm?
He seems to understand whatever I'm referencing,\n
even though it was just a shot in the dark.
Ah, then you must be from the nearby village...
Y-Yes, there you have it!
That explains it then. Fine work you're doing.
Their leader gives me an approving nod.\n
It doesn't look like he doubts me at all...
He's even praising us for our efforts.
I'm sorry to put you through all this. Still,\n
we should have them driven back to their land\n
soon.
Th-That is most relieving to hear!\n
But I heard that the Yamatan soldiers are\n
really strong...
It seems they believed us to be backwater\n
bumpkins. They were all talk and no skill.
Some have genuine ability, but the majority are\n
mere novices. And their commander is simply\n
hopeless.
Hopeless?
What was his name again? Something like Deppa...\n
Dekopachi, maybe, or Degarashi...?
Wait, Dekopompo...!? I mean--I believe there\n
was a general by such, er, name.
Yes, that's it! You certainly are well-informed.
Anyhow, his name doesn't really matter.
Th-That was a close one.\n
Almost blew my cover there.
So this Dekopachi guy yells out his name like\n
an idiot when he shows up in battle.\n
Everyone knows it by now.
Well, you clearly haven't remembered it...
Yes, the commander is a lost cause. I know\n
they're the enemy, but you really have to pity\n
his soldiers...
We just provoke him, and he charges blindly into\n
our hidden mud pits. It's worked three times\n
now.
I-Is that so...
He just always falls for it! We're honestly\n
starting to wonder if it's part of some scheme\n
of his.
He is a disgrace to all of Yamato...
I don't know why, but... I feel like crying...
They should be running out of supplies soon,\n
and their patience is likely running thin.
They may go for an all-out assault if they get\n
too desperate. Be careful on your way.
Th-Thank you. We will.
As I nod in agreement, I feel something prodding\n
at my knees.
I look over to see Nekone, trying to send me a\n
message with her eyes alone.
...Yeah, I know. Staying here won't do us any\n
good. We should get a move on before someone\n
slips up.
W-Well, we will be going on our way now, then.
Katana_mesh
Saya_mesh
I end the conversation and turn back to the\n
others.
Jachdwalt sees my intent, and goes to push the\n
carts back on the road, when--
Hey.
I jump a little, not expecting to be directly\n
called to.
Y-Yes? Is there something else...?
I look back in fear, but the leader stands\n
there with an easy smile.
The road here is pretty uneven. It'll be hard\n
setting the carts on your own. Men, we assist\n
them!
N-No need, my good sir. I would not want to\n
get in your way...
It's fine. Don't worry about it--we need to\n
help each other when we're in need, right?
The soldiers ignore my words and approach the\n
carts... but one of them pauses, sounding\n
unsure.
I follow the soldier's gaze to Kuon, who is\n
determinedly looking in the opposite direction.
Wh--Kuon!!
She's acting way too suspicious.
And of course, the soldier walks over to where\n
Kuon is, trying to get a look at her face.
I swear I've seen you before...
Kuon's neck strains slightly as she avoids the\n
peering eyes of the soldier.
The soldier continues to step around her,\n
trying to get a good look at her face.
Gradually, the other Tuskur soldiers notice\n
this strange scene.
Hey, I know she's pretty, but that's enough\n
bothering the lady!
This is why you never get any girls, y'know!
Th-That's not what this is about!
The soldier reddens as the other men in the unit\n
taunt him, and he yells back defensively.
I swear I've seen her before... Not in my\n
village, but at a festival after I moved to\n
the capital...?
He pauses a moment longer, still in thought,\n
but seems to recall something in a sudden jolt.
Head
I-I remember now! Are you--!?\n
But... you CAN'T be--
Tch...!
K-Kuon...
Sh-She just chopped him right in the neck...
He's not dead, but he's definitely out cold.
Kuon hastily crouches down, and sits the\n
unconscious soldier up as she begins to rub\n
his shoulders vigorously.
A-Aha... Ahahaha... H-His shoulders looked a\n
little stiff, you know...?
But the soldier's eyes have completely rolled up\n
into his head, his body flopping limply.
Ah... um...
Everyone's expression is frozen. The area goes\n
completely silent.
The first one to snap back to reality is their\n
leader. He shouts, pointing an accusing finger.
Y-You're from Yamato, aren't you!?
D-Dear sister!?
Hah... I suppose we could not deceive the keen\n
eyes of Tuskur warriors after all! Well spotted!
Hee hee! Finally, things are picking up a bit.
It would seem she has given up.
"Well spotted" my ASS!
